one_liner: protoc plugin generating reflection-free Marshal/Unmarshal/Size/Equal/Clone helpers for Go protobuf APIv2; ~1.7x faster unmarshal than stock protoc-gen-go.
what_it_does: vtprotobuf is protoc-gen-go-vtproto, a second protoc plugin that runs alongside the standard protoc-gen-go (APIv2) and emits auxiliary *_vtproto.pb.go files per message: SizeVT, MarshalVT/MarshalToVT/MarshalToSizedBufferVT, UnmarshalVT/UnmarshalVTUnsafe, EqualVT, CloneVT, and optional pool helpers (ResetVT/ReturnToVTPool/FromVTPool). It does not replace the standard proto.Marshal/proto.Unmarshal reflection-based codec; call sites must explicitly call the VT-suffixed methods, or the RPC layer must register vtprotobuf's provided gRPC, DRPC, or Twirp codec to use them transparently.
how_it_is_fast: All (de)serialization logic is fully unrolled per-field at codegen time (ported from gogo/protobuf's approach to the APIv2 API), so there is no reflection walk over the message descriptor at runtime. SizeVT precomputes the exact encoded size so MarshalVT allocates its output buffer once. UnmarshalVTUnsafe casts wire bytes directly into string/[]byte fields instead of copying them. The optional generated sync.Pool-backed object pools (ResetVT/ReturnToVTPool/FromVTPool) let callers reuse whole message structs across unmarshal calls, avoiding allocation entirely, which is where most of the reported speedup comes from.
when_to_use: Go services already on google.golang.org/protobuf (APIv2) with (de)serialization visible as CPU cost in profiles (RPC hot paths, replication/streaming row processing).
gRPC, DRPC, or Twirp services that can install vtprotobuf's provided codec so all messages benefit without touching call sites.
Teams that can explicitly opt into memory pooling per message type and manage single-owner reuse lifetime carefully, where most of the >10x gain reported by the author lives.
Want reflection-free CloneVT/EqualVT/SizeVT even without wiring the whole RPC path.
Comfortable checking in generated *_vtproto.pb.go files as part of the normal protoc build step.
when_not_to_use: Still generating APIv1/gogo code: vtprotobuf targets APIv2 only and is explicitly not compatible with APIv1-generated code per the README.

Can't tolerate unsafe byte aliasing: UnmarshalVTUnsafe pins the entire input buffer alive via GC for the life of any string/bytes field taken from the message (open issue #167), which can silently balloon retained memory if a field is cached long-term.
Messages are small or short-lived: the author's own post notes many protobuf messages are too small for pooling to help, and the ~1.7x codegen-only gain (no pooling) is the realistic floor.

Need pooling correctness for repeated fields, maps, or nested messages: multiple open issues report pooled ResetVT/ReturnToVTPool bugs with repeated fields (#92) and note pooling only reaches the outer message, not nested children (#162, 'Recursive Pool Usage').
Want a single drop-in replacement for proto.Marshal/Unmarshal with zero call-site changes and no RPC codec registration step.

integration.dependencies: google.golang.org/protobuf (APIv2) required; optional integration deps on google.golang.org/grpc, storj.io/drpc, or github.com/twitchtv/twirp for the provided codecs
integration.min_toolchain: go.mod pins `go 1.26.4` to build the plugin/runtime as of the last commit; the `unique` string-interning field option additionally needs Go 1.23+ in consumer code
integration.platforms: any (pure Go, no architecture-specific code in the repo tree)
integration.thread_safety: not documented for generated Marshal/Unmarshal methods beyond standard protobuf message rules (safe for concurrent reads, not for concurrent mutation); pooled objects are explicitly single-owner — using a message after ReturnToVTPool() is undefined behavior per the README
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: generates extra *_vtproto.pb.go files next to standard protoc-gen-go output; existing proto.Marshal/Unmarshal call sites keep working unchanged and must be explicitly switched to the VT-suffixed methods (or the RPC codec must be registered) to see any speedup

gotchas: UnmarshalVTUnsafe keeps the whole input wire buffer alive via GC for as long as any string/bytes field from the message is reachable (unsafe.String aliasing); documented as an open gap in issue #167, not yet in the README.
UnmarshalVT on a non-zeroed message behaves like proto.Merge rather than a fresh Unmarshal; call Reset() first or use a freshly allocated message.

Memory pooling is opt-in per message (`option (vtproto.mempool)` or `--go-vtproto_opt=pool=...`) and, as of issue #162, only pools the outer message — nested/child messages are still freshly allocated on each unmarshal.
Returning a pooled repeated-field message has open correctness bugs (issue #92, generated ResetVT); verify pool behavior with your own message shapes before relying on it in production.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The catalogued siblings (RapidProto, Zserio, FlatBuffers) are all C++ alternatives to protoc's C++ output; pick vtprotobuf instead whenever the stack is Go on google.golang.org/protobuf APIv2, since it optimizes protoc's existing Go codegen and wire format rather than replacing either.
verified_claims_summary: Per the author's 2021 Vitess blog post (Vicent Marti), a synthetic VReplication stress test replicating a large MySQL table between keyspaces measured 7.17 CPU-seconds of unmarshal overhead with stock protoc-gen-go (APIv2) vs 4.15 CPU-seconds with vtprotobuf's UnmarshalVT (~1.7x), falling to 0.63 CPU-seconds (~11x) when vtprotobuf's generated memory pooling is also used; the post gives no hardware, Go version, or compiler flags, and the repo ships no benchmark code to reproduce the numbers.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-07-02, 1118 stars, used in production by Vitess/PlanetScale and widely adopted in the Go gRPC ecosystem); BSD-3-Clause and small enough to vendor, but 'copyable' here means installing the plugin and wiring it into your protoc invocation, not literally copying a header.
